You see 4 top-down photoreal renderings of the same room labelled SCENE A, SCENE B, SCENE C, SCENE D. Geometry, doors and windows are identical; only furniture differs.

Rank the scenes from BEST to WORST by overall arrangement quality. First reason briefly inside `<reasoning>...</reasoning>`, then output a single permutation of the labels inside `<answer>...</answer>` (no separators, no ties).
For THIS bounded diagnostic, rank by these explicit priorities: fewer outside-floor objects first; then fewer new wall intersections; then fewer newly introduced furniture intersections; then prefer a verified B planar witness; then fewer remaining furniture intersections. Do not infer object absence from occlusion: every candidate retains the listed same 9 object IDs. These checks do not establish human comfort or preference.
Original B brief:
